name: P-058 typed owned-container inspection and absence reconciliation
timestampEvidence: Suite start is approximately log mtime minus reported node:test duration; actual absence timestamps come from its saved measured receipt. These are separate runs.
summary: Conventional suite passed 123 tests with no failures, cancellations or skips. New absent immutable-container regression first failed on old source for both Docker and Podman, then passed. The maintained helper subsequently confirmed the already-removed exact profile5 container absent in 129 ms and left its original receipt unchanged. No ARM workload or daemon restart was launched.

actualAbsence.scope: Absence-only lookup of the already-removed immutable profile5 container via the maintained typed helper; no create, start, or removal.

regression.newCase: reconciliation settles an absent immutable container without generic inspect fallback
regression.redBeforeFix: Current continuation executed the new case before the source change; Docker and Podman subtests failed with ETIMEDOUT inspecting another object namespace.

assertions.evidence: All three known-container reads use --type container; producer and boot fixtures enforce the namespace.
New Docker and Podman regressions persist removed:true, cleanupPending:false and clear the stale cleanup error after one absent lookup.
Complete 123-test suite retained image/token matching, late-create reconciliation, foreign-owner refusal and cleanup-failure behavior.

The structured actualAbsence receipt above records the maintained helper's absence-only lookup of immutable container 00325c4beccc61e2f3cdd175b2b5ff981ffd85cb4985210faf3e7344aae432d9 in 129 ms: removed:true, cleanupPending:false, originalReceiptUnchanged:true. Original receipt SHA-256 remains 728f8c748f548d8e3e9efda5da4b29716c54575051ac33640db787e672bbb7b7. No create, start, or removal occurred.

limitations: The Docker generic-inspect fallback internals were not traced; the paired same-endpoint reads isolate namespace selection as the cleanup defect.
Original ARM boot timeout and Docker create/start delay remain separate open work.
No installed-native or final release acceptance is established.
